item.title: The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants from Mastery Pack: Assassin
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|collecting|finance

The 10 Chase Cards Everybody Wants from Mastery Pack: Assassin

Don't let powerful cards sneak up on you! Flesh and Blood's latest Mastery Pack is stuffed with must-have cards.

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 13, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

Guys, gals and non-binary pals: the doctor is in.  

Even better, he's not the only one. Mastery Pack: Assassin is the latest instalment of Flesh and Blood's increasingly popular ancillary booster sets, designed to provide everything that fans of the Assassin class will need to get into the class, upgrade their decks and inflict crippling diseases on their opponent. 

It might just be the most important Mastery Pack so far. Mastery Pack: Assassin not only revitalizes neglected heroes like Uzuri, Switchblade and Arakni, Huntsman, but introduces the horrific Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits into the Classic Constructed format. It's also the foundation for Outbreak, the first booster set of 2027. That's some awfully big boots to fill...

...and don't worry. I'll have an Armory Deck upgrade guide for Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits for you next week. I'm in the kitchen myself, hang tight for a minute.

Somehow, Mastery Pack: Assassin has a little something for everyone despite clearly being tailored towards fans of the stabby stabby. If you're already deeply intrenched in the class, you're obviously covered — but there's also timely reprints for players entering the class for the first time and a handful of generics that'll fit into any collection. That's to say nothing of the high-end marvel collectibles. There's something for everyone in here!

So, what should you be hoping to find when you pop open those packs in the coming days? I'm glad you asked, mysterious voice on the internet. Here's some of my top picks for the most coveted cards from Flesh and Blood's Mastery Pack: Assassin. 

#10: Outbreak

You are not high enough on this card. There. I said it.  

Outbreak is the kind of card that's obviously powerful, but it's difficult to grasp how ubiquitous it has the potential to be until you've got a couple of games in. It's the golden rule in Flesh and Blood: "Blue block-threes that you actually want to play sometimes are kind of busted"

I think Outbreak is clearly at its best in Dr Mortimer, who can cure one of the ineffectual diseases to generate Silver, but a reaction that'll be worth upwards of five points of value that's so easily pitch stacked is appealing to any assassin. Taking all the tempo from your opponent with on-hits also lends itself towards cards that allow you to convert your full hand, which is exactly what Outbreak will allow you to do. 

#9: Banger!

You can't call a card Banger! and not design it as a certified banger.  

This card is horrific in the endgame when life totals begin to plummet, but it's also potentially quite strong as a blue that Uzuri, Switchblade is interested in switching in. If the opponent underblocks? Great, you're hitting for seven. If they overblock? Just leave your small attack on the chain and cash Banger! in for a Silver.

I'm also in love with the idea of pitch stacking a copy of this card next to a couple of Just a Nick, or sleeving it up in Kayo, Underhanded Cheat as a sweet target for your hero ability. It's so difficult to end up with a positive exchange for the opponent regardless of if they block or not.

I'm expecting Banger! to be a solid role player in several decks, so I'd suggest snapping up some copies while you can.  

#8: Remember the Mists

I feel similar ways about Remember the Mists as I do about Outbreak. While it's clearly at its best in a particular assassin, it's probably good enough to see universal play as a flexible blue with upside.  

Remember the Mists is Surgical Extraction at home. While you can't always rip away a meaningful card from the opposing hand, you can seriously mess with arrows and blue cards that the opponent intended to pitch away to fuel their turn. If you're really lucky, you'll find a pesky fabled gem in their hand and send it into the abyss forever.  

Despite the obvious power in Uzuri, I think Remember the Mists is also a meaningful upgrade to Arakni, Huntsman. The deck typically relies on Surgical Extraction to remove the final cards from the hand of an opponent that you're trying to fatigue. Remember the Mists provides another three blues that achieve the same thing, which is a pretty big boon in my book.  

#7: Expense Not Spared 

This card reads like Swordmaster's Shine just chugged an energy drink, but I actually think it's entirely fine at time of writing. Silver is a finite resource for many of these heroes and should be seen as a real cost to play Expense Not Spared.

Think about it this way: the floor for two silver is rebuying a Graven Gloves (or similar piece in a different slot), so we should consider two Silver to be worth at least two value. If you squint, that makes Expense Not Spared more of a +3 than a +5. That's still quite good, but it makes those comparisons to other cards a little misleading.  

The power of this card will come in forcing through on-hits. The best possible fork is having Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits active as you attack to convince your opponent that you're looking for Go Again, then whacking them over the head with five damage at reaction speed instead.

#6: Important Assassin Reprints

I'm going to cobble a few of these together into one entry, so they don't eat up my entire list. The fact I need to consider doing that is a good sign for the health of Mastery Pack: Assassin.   

It's no secret that several of the staple assassin threats were getting a little expensive as the hype for Mastery Pack: Assassin and Outbreak began to swell. While this product didn't quite manage to tackle all those price increases (it was never going to), it does contain many important ones for players getting into Assassin.  

Persuasive Prognosis, Pain in the Backside and Blacktek Whisperers are staples of the class and should be cheaper than they have been in a long time in the immediate wake of release. There's no better time to purchase them if you've been sitting on your hands. 

#5: Phial of Calamity

It takes a really potent piece of kit to usurp a dagger, but I think Phial of Calamity has such a terrifying threat of activation is specific matchups that the juice will be worth the squeeze.  

In aggressive matchups where the opponent doesn't want to block, this says "if you ignore my dagger, your arsenal is gone". In Assassin/Ranger matchups, on-demand Frailty is both your best friend and fuels half the cost to get Phail of Calamity back into play. It also causes headaches once your opponent is sitting at three life because of Bloodrot Pox.  

In Arakni, 5L!p3d 7hRu 73h cR4X, I think this card is kind of heinous. Kiss of Death gets to double dip on whatever affliction you decided to afflict thanks to Flick Knives.  If you do that multiple times in a game? Disgusting. 

#4: Silver (Marvel)

Despite being the least flashy card on this list, the marvel variant of the Silver token is very flashy in real life. That's exactly why everybody is going to want it.  

Silver is slowly becoming an important part of every assassin's toolkit, and most Flesh and Blood players are magpies. If my deck makes Silver, I need the nice one or I'm a disgrace to my class. It really is as simple as that.  

#3: Cadaver Handlers

I'm down for you to quote me on this one. Cadaver Handlers are not only the best card in Mastery Pack: Assassin: they're one of the top five equipment ever printed.  

This thing is NUTS. It's never been more difficult to block a Codex of Frailty into a Leave No Witnesses. Cadaver Handlers effects the whole chain link for some reason, so even if you hold your defense reaction until after it's been activated, it'll still get shrunk.

Thankfully, that does mean that it won't break Temper equipment that hadn't blocked before, but that seems like a small reprieve. I bought a cold foil yesterday because I believe this card is stupid. I really can't think a better endorsement than that.  

#2: Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits (Marvel)

In the era of FaB 3.0, I get the feeling that adult hero marvels are going to become a hot commodity. Frankly, they already were. Have you seen the price on Viserai, the Forsaken lately?!  

The vibe on Dr.Mortimer, Blight of the Pits heading into release is pretty darn good. There are high expectations for the hero straight out of the gate and an army of fans who love the Assassin class. I'm expecting the premium version of his adult hero card to become a small goldmine if he lives up to his potential.  

It shouldn't hit the highs of the Jarl Vetreidi marvel, but frankly it doesn't need to. 

#1: Dynasty Attack Marvels

But these might. What an absurd introduction to FAB 3.0!

Leave No Witnesses and Surgical Extraction have been a core part of Assassin's identity since the class first released back in Dynasty, while Eradicate has seen a strong amount of play for the weakest card in the cycle. This trio is assassin. It makes so much sense to give them the premium treatment as the headliner for this set. 

These are all going to be grails for collectors and players alike, but I'm expecting Leave No Witnesses to be in a league of its own. It's been a three of in every Assassin deck since it was printed, so those serious assassin players are going to see it as an incredibly worthwhile investment.

item.title: Off-Meta Minute: Amber Amethyst Merida
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|competitive

Off-Meta Minute: Amber Amethyst Merida

Muuuuuum! It's just my bow!

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Deck diversity has always been an appealing part of card games for me. As a competitor, I tend to prefer narrower metagames that are easier for me to target, but as a person? Let me turn up to my weekly event and play against every different flavor of nonsense out there. I wanna see what kind of brew gets you out of bed in the morning.

That's a big part of why I started Off-Meta Minute here on TCGplayer. If you cook up something cool, you deserve your flowers. Somehow, I have the platform to give them to you while also encouraging up-and-coming Illumineers to give your madness a shot. It's one of the coolest parts of my job.

Sometimes it's difficult to give the right person flowers, though. Sometimes, a sweet archetype pops up, and I cannot quite place where it originally came from as it lights up the tournament tables like wildfire.

That's what happened with Amber Amethyst Merida.

ELJ_GHartuck's Amber Amethyst Merida - 186th Place at Disney Lorcana Challenge Villain Challenge: Gaston 

I'd also like to mention Liam Dolecki's Top 256 performance with this archetype in DLC London's Main Event 1. The deck clearly has competitive legs; I just like GHartuck's list a little better.

This deck is a side grade to the more popular variants of Amber Amethyst with a few cute tricks baked in. We'll start with the namesake card, Merida - Wisp Conjurer.

 

We don't get Merlin - Rabbit or Genie - Wish Fulfilled anymore, but you can still accelerate into a pair of four-cost Amethyst characters that can draw you cards. You can lean on Mickey Mouse - Best in Town or Hamm - Piggy Bank within your first two turns to curve cleanly into a copy of Merlin - Profoundly Curious (who refunds you for the help) or a difficult-to-contest Merida - Wisp Conjurer that immediately draws a card and threatens to snowball out of control.

 

The best follow-up to Merida is often just a second copy, who can enter play exerted to draw you two cards in tandem with her counterpart. That's not enough to build a deck around though, so you'll need to rely on some other friends to help maximize the number of cards you can score from Merida. How do you do that? Bodyguard.

Rex - Protective Dinosaur is the best cheap bodyguard in this ink combination, regularly trading up for bigger characters and scoring you some lore in the process. Lionheart - Incumbent Mayor is an absolute tank with impossibly difficult stats to push through. Both will gain you incidental lore while banking cards of Merida, leading to an opponent who is frantically trying to bust through the wall to stop the card advantage while falling further and further behind.

But my favorite piece of spice? Remember Me. In those long, grindy games, it's not uncommon for an opponent to think they're running you out of cards before a Merida and a Hamm sing this backbreaking song, allowing you to play like three characters from your discard exerted and draw a card off every single one. You don't want to draw too many of these, so I like having only a single copy — but it's an army in a can all by itself.

 

I alluded to it briefly when talking about Rex and Lionheart, but this deck can close the door shockingly fast once those cards get spinning. Merlin's Shop and Smithy - Magical Market is an annoyingly sticky location that you can ferry your characters to for some extra lore and card draw. Even better, nobody wants to waste their time removing it. Once you enter the late game with a bucket of leftover ink drops, sometimes it'll just be sitting there waiting to win the game. It's a snazzy piece of cardboard.

I also wanted to mention how well the Demona - Imperious Spellcaster package slots into this deck. Of course, the namesake variant is a beast of a card by itself. It'll happily discard one of those cards you've drawn to turn into a turbocharged Madam Mim - Fox, but it can also fill the discard for a timely Remember Me in this shell. Demona - Betrayer of the Clan is also a phenomenal character to accelerate into with Hamm - Piggy Bank against aggressive decks and loves to be juiced up with Rush.

But the high roll? Use Demona - Scourge of the Wyvern Clan to lock down the opposing board before the Imperious Spellcaster sends her rushing into battle. I've had a handful of games where I've been able to play both of these cards with Remember Me and proceeded to blast my opponent's board to bits. It's very sweet.

Closing Thoughts 

I'm very glad that the Hyperia City metagame continues to offer some room to breathe for players who aren't enamored with Amber Emerald or Emerald Steel. Merida - Wisp Conjurer is an absurdly sweet card that didn't really get any time in the sun when it was released back in Attack of the Vine!, so I'm overjoyed to see players cooking up deck lists that allow her to shine. Is Remember Me the sauce? I don't know for sure, but I can't help but hope.

Have further questions? Let me know over at @HowlingMines on X (formerly Twitter) or @howlingmines.com over on Bluesky! Alternatively, give my other work here on TCGplayer a peek if you'd like another slice of everything nice about your favorite game. 

But until next time. I've been HowlingMines, you've been amazing! 

Stay safe out there — and happy gaming!

item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026
item.description:
Pokémon|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026

You can't keep a good cat down.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

I know it's trendy to talk these days about how the Pokémon market is slowing down. About how some of the market is correcting, about how many more cards are printed these days, and about how there's just no future in modern Pokémon chase hits.

And then Delta Reign released, and we watched Raikou ex leap up in price.

Delta Reign Defies the Dip

Will this Raikou ex hold the $105 Market Price it has today long-term? Maybe not. But even as more Delta Reign has entered the market over the last week, we've seen the price of the Special Illustration Rare climb in price, and quite drastically. That $105 Market Price tag it carries today is way up from the $90 it was coming out of the gate last week. Clearly, there's still demand for new Pokémon cards, at least high quality Illustration Rare and Special Illustration Rare cards like Raikou.

Elsewhere in Delta Reign, things are progressing more as expected. The headliner SIR Mega Rayquaza ex is actually outpacing the gold version of the same, and both are sliding down slowly in price since release. The gold version (MHR Mega Rayquaza has predictably slid from $225 down to $210 over the last week, while the true chase of the set, Mega Rayquaza, has dipped slightly from $310 down to under $300.

On the other hand, IR Kecleon has been a bit of a surprise winner from the set, moving from $23 at its low to closer to $30+ today. It's easy to see why, given such beautiful artwork on the seldom-seen Pokémon. Similarly, Mega Golisopod ex 135 has actually inched up from $20 to $25 in that same time.

So if you were wondering whether the unlucky set that had to follow 30th Celebration would have its own share of hits, it looks like Delta Reign didn't disappoint in that regard.

Old Promos Spike Unexpectedly

Mewtwo-EX XY125 originally was available in a Super-Premium Collection, back in 2016. Since then, it's been a very slow—but very steady—climb up to its current all-time high Market Price. Once available for as low as $5, Mewtwo-EX had climbed up to $30 by the time 2025 rolled around—and then more than doubled to $75 by the start of 2026. Somehow, it's only gained steam since.

The current run on Mewtwo-EX began around the end of the summer, when the card first began to push up to the $100 threshold, only to keep going. After yet another strong first half of a month, we saw the Market Price on Mewtwo-EX XY125 push all the way up to a new all-time high of nearly $200, with live Near Mint listings stretching even beyond that.

I don't know if it was the Lugia focus from the Classic Collection in 30th Celebration that started the ball rolling on the Reverse Holofoil Lugia from 2016's Fates Collide, but it's gaining speed now. The card started the summer out at just around $5, but has been on an incredible run ever since. It first climbed up to $10 around September, and this week has begun to push even higher as copies slowly dwindle. Like many older (or in this case, mid-era) cards, the movement here is halting, but it is emblematic of where much of the market is putting its focus these days.

New Promos Predictably Drop

Speaking of cards dropping in price, the 2026 McDonald's set of cards is out and the prices are falling fast, with nothing fetching more than $5 (predictably, Pikachu takes 1st place). These limited-release runs can sometimes get pretty pricey, especially years later, so if you're trying to get a little weird with it and catch all the Pokémon you can inside a Happy Meal, you can complete the release quite easily right now.

And while we are on the subject of promos…

A futuristic Pikachu and a gorgeous piece of Espeon art featuring multiple cameos from other Pokémon? That's a slam dunk of a duo, and both of these new releases are available for an ever-more affordable price. 

As they come out of the gate and the market settles, it looks like Pikachu ex has settled around $20-$25, while Espeon ex is coming in closer to $30. With 30th Celebration product still being rolled out and promos still hitting the market, it's difficult to predict exactly where these go from here, but the price for those collecting 30th Celebration is looking quite affordable—especially compared to those $3,000 RBG Mews.

Ascended Heroes and Destined Rivals Continue to Fall

Finally, let's look at the biggest drop of 2026—coming after the climb of 2026—in Ascended Heroes. The set was full of hits and hugely hyped when it was released, and then things began to climb even higher from there. Mega Gengar ex was once pushing $1,400.

Times have changed, as mass reprints of this and other 2026 sets have absolutely cratered prices on the biggest hits in the set. There's nothing to scoff at in a $550 Mega Gengar ex, but that's down $50 in Market Price this week, and obviously worlds away from $1,400. Similarly, Pikachu ex dropped from $560 down to $520. Of course, it's all relative—these are still insanely good hits from a booster pack.

The same goes for SIR Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex from Destined Rivals, the Team Rocket-focused set that is stacked with cool designs. It also had one of several mega chase cards in Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex, but reprints have similarly brought prices down. This week Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex dropped from $310 to $280. 

Until next week, good luck pulling Rayquaza from your Delta Reign!

item.title: The Top 10 Most Underrated Cards You Missed From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|competitive

The Top 10 Most Underrated Cards You Missed From Yu-Gi-Oh's Magnificent Maestros

Instead of hunting for high-value Grand Master Rares, maybe pick up some Dragons and some Witches!

By Hanko Chow

|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

10 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

Another highly anticipated Magnificent set is finally here, bringing players more opportunities to pull those luxurious Serialized Grand Master Rares or those Overframe Starlights/Ultra Rares! Aside from shiny cardboard, many players are super stoked for the brand new Toon cards that are revolutionizing the metagame Mind Scan and insane search power.

The Most Underrated Cards From Magnificent Maestros

Blue-Eyes, Rokkets and Toon cards are surely the fan-favorite picks out of this new set, but there's also a surprising amount of other new support cards you can't forget. Let's take a look at some of the underrated cards you may have missed!

#10 Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon

This new Link-5 monster is reminiscent of the Five-Headed Link Dragon, one of the earliest Link-5's created with 5000 ATK and something to do with multiple attributes while being almost invincible. Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon is much better though! For starters, you can use another Link-5 monster by itself to Link Summon Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon. That's probably why they had to preemptively nerf it by Limiting the card before release. Otherwise, all the best combo decks would surely play three copies to perform some sort of FTK combo since it has a burn effect on summon. Inflicting the opponent 300 damage for every Link monster in your graveyard surely adds up pretty fast, especially if it used itself to summon another.

Luckily the R&D team made the right decision to limit Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon to prevent said scenario, but that doesn't mean it isn't good anymore. It's still a great option in any deck that can put up enough bodies to make a Link-5 for the board wipe effect and high damage capabilities. If your deck already includes Underworld Goddess of the Closed World, you might as well throw in a copy of Perfectron Hydradrive Dragon to close out the game.

#9 Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl

Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl plays a bit differently than its Crimson Dragon counterpart. Where Crimson Dragon needs another Synchro on the field to change its form, Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl needs another Dragon Synchro to negate a monster effect, but Quetzalcoatl also reborns all your Dragon Synchros on summon! This makes me think you want to use your Dragon Synchros alongside a Tuner to make Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl since it'll just reborn it back anyways on summon.

I wonder if Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl has a place in Centur-Ions since that strategy loves making Level 12 Synchros and bringing back Centur-Ion Auxila does seem pretty decent. Alternatively, maybe Quetzalcoatl is better in Blue-Eyes since it's possible to make it with the help of Neo Kaiser Sea Horse and a Blue-Eyes White Dragon. I wouldn't be surprised if it's also an end board piece to the Red Dragon Archfiend deck. As long as it takes a bunch of monsters to make alongside another Dragon Synchro, I don't think we'll see Crimson Dragon Quetzalcoatl as a way to "beat" Nibiru, the Primal Being anytime soon, but it does however force it out of the opponent's hand.

#8 Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul

The newest form of Red Dragon Archfiend, or more specifically Red Nova Dragon, Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul is very similar to its original form by being a huge indestructible Dragon Synchro, but with a twist! You can Synchro Summon this new Dragon properly by using two Tuners and any non-tuners that add up to Level 12, or you can banish any two Tuners regardless of levels and a monster that's named Red Dragon Archfiend to summon it from the Extra Deck. Think of it like Black-Winged Assault Dragon except you need two Tuners.

When you summon Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul, you can activate its effect to add back any card from your graveyard to your hand! Think of it like Firewall Dragon or Constellar Ptolemy M7, except it's not limited to just monsters. Now you combine this ability with another effect that can send something to the graveyard, and you'll see how Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul is pretty busted.

By using Red Lotus King, Flame Crime to send one of the broken Virus Traps to the graveyard (either Eradicator Epidemic Virus, Deck Devastation Virus or Full Force Virus), you can then add it back later on with Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul, which also fulfils the requirement to use those Virus cards. I'm sure there's a ton of other Traps you can find to abuse this combo like Magic Deflector or Different Dimension Ground.

#7 Starving Venom Fusion Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons

Predaplants or Super Polymerization is getting another fantastic Fusion to summon with Starving Venom Fusion Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons. This new form takes the same materials as the original Starving Venom Fusion Dragons but it's also treated as a Predaplant card which is a pretty cool flavor for the archetype.

If your opponent has three Dark monsters on the field, you may be tempted to use Super Polymerization to make Predaplant Triphyoverutum right away. However, you should consider summoning this latest Dragon instead since it can negate the monster left on the field while changing it's ATK to zero. Later on, it can perform another Fusion Summon using the monsters on either field including itself, allowing you to wait for your opponent to commit another Dark monster and then using all of them to summon Predaplant Triphyoverutum that way.

#6 Future Fusion Nova

Cyber Dragons get a new Fusion Spell that reminiscent of Brilliant Fusion since it's a Continuous Fusion Spell that instantly summons the monster by using materials from your deck. The downside is that you're then restricted to summoning only Machine monsters and can't attack except with the monster you summoned. These restrictions are very managable especially if you're going first with it.

Future Fusion Nova doesn't just summon any Fusion though. You're instead restricted to only summoning a Light Machine Fusion and you must include a copy of Cyber Dragon as one of the Fusion Materials. After combing through the card database for all the viable Light Machine Fusion monsters, there are surprisingly a decent number of choices.

For starters, you can summon Invoked Mechaba by using an Aleister the Invoker and Cyber Dragon from your Deck, giving you a negate right away so your other cards can resolve. Union Controller just needs either Y-Yare Head or Z-Zillion Tank alongside Cyber Dragon and gives access to Union Hangar or Unauthorized Reactivation for the ABC-Dragon Buster deck. Lastly, the new Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon is thematically a fantastic option since it's an OTK machine by itself, but it's also a Level 10 Machine that can be viable for the Train deck.

#5 Lightning Crash

A new search spell is always welcomed to the TCG. Just look at what happened to Bonfire when it first came out. We might not have a dominating Thunder deck right now, but it's only a matter of time before we do. At present, Blitzclique is a competent deck when it snowballs into advantage and Sacred Beast can always make use for more copies of Calamity of the Sacred Beasts - Hamon, Lord of Striking Thunder. They both might be a bit gatekept by Mind Scan right now, but it doesn't hurt to have a playset of Lightning Crash just in case.

If you're looking for other Thunder monsters, you may want to consider the Thunder Dragons if you just want to increase your hand size with Thunder Dragon, or somehow bridge yourself a way to Thunder Dragon Colossus with Thunder Dragondark and Thunder Dragonhawk. Sword Ryzeal is a Thunder as well, and while it may not be able to be Normal Summoned because of Lightning Crash, any two other Level 4's can make Ryzeal Duo Drive to help summon that Sword.

Maybe you want to revisit your Spright deck since those are all Thunders that can be Special Summoned if you control a Level 2. The free bodies you can get off Spright Blue and Spright Jet can help Link climb, or you might just want access to Spright Red to fend off a monster effect.

#4 Demiurge Ema

Monarch's newest support card isn't a Monarch card at all. Demiurge Ema is a Level 8 Fairy that just so happens to send monsters with the "Monarch stats" to the graveyard, more specifically 2400 or more ATK and exactly 1000 DEF. Players are calling Demiurge Ema the "Monarch Circular" as a reference to Mathmech Circular even though Magicians' Souls was released earlier than Circular.

Demiurge Ema is very powerful as it enables a one-card combo for Zaborg the Mega Monarch, which can usually win the game on the spot. It just requires you to either play Monarchs or a few other cards that you must send for Demiurge Ema - namely, two copies of Photon Emperor, Zaborg the Mega Monarch and a copy of Erebus the Underworld Monarch.

Photon Emperor coincidentally meets the requirement for Demiurge Ema. After you send both copies to the graveyard, one of the Photon Emperors will trigger since it was sent to the graveyard while you control the other Photon Emperor in the grave. This gives you a free Special Summon that just so happens to also be a Level 8 and Light attribute. Now you just need to pitch a Monarch Spell or Trap for Erebus's effect to retrieve Zaborg the Mega Monarch and you have exactly what you need to summon it!

You could also use Demiurge Ema and Photon Emperor for a Rank 8 play like Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord to defend yourself from a monster hand trap like Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring if you already opened with other Monarch combo pieces.

#3, 2 and 1 Witchcrafter cards!

Witchcrafter is getting seven new support cards in this set, all of which are pretty insane for the strategy, but I'll just highlight three of them since they're the most important cards in the new Witchcrafter deck.

Witchcrafter Walpurgis not only gives the deck another monster search but it's basically Brain Research Lab but for Witchcrafters. This means Witchcrafter monsters can bypass their required costs of discarding a Spell from hand by sending a Spell from deck instead. We've seen what happened in the past when Brain Research Lab was legal with a card like Mind Master (with its original effect), so it's a matter of time before players realize how busted these new Spellcaster cards are when you play with other themes.

You can get Walpurgis very consistently thanks to Witchcrafter Marka, which is also searchable off Witchcrafter Creation or summonable off various Witchcrafter monsters and Verre Magic - Lacrima of Light. By tributing Marka from hand or field, you get to add Walpurgis or Witchcrafter Bystreet for some destruction protection. Then when Marka is in the graveyard and sees a Witchcrafter leave the field by your opponent's card effect, it can reborn itself and tribute an opponent's monster to take revenge for the fallen Witchcrafter. Marka also just so happens to be a Dark Level 6 Spellcaster which allows you to bridge with Dark Magician of Destruction. Overall, Witchcrafter Marka does a lot for this deck.

All these new Witchcrafter cards are a cause for Witchcrafter Celebration! The deck has a chance to be high tier thanks to its fix on consistency and costs while also having a new way to Fusion Summon thanks to Witchcrafter Celebration. A common combo you'll see is Witchcrafter Genni copying Witchcrafter Celebration so the Fusion Summon will shuffle back the banished Spellcasters into the deck to be reused on another turn. Then, Witchcrafter Pupils will recycle Witchcrafter Celebration back to your graveyard  and, if you didn't use Witchcrafter Celebration that turn, you can add it back to your hand. This way, Witchcrafter Pupils can copy the effect of Witchcrafter Celebration during your opponent's turn as another form of disruption!

The other new Witchcrafter cards are also great, like the aforementioned Witchcrafter Pupils for the Celebration combo. You can't go wrong with an omni-negate Counter Trap in Witchcrafter Distortion, and Witchcrafter Terracottan is another method of Fusion Summoning while also helping recycle a Witchcrafter card to your hand. Witchcrafter Madame Rilliona is a bit situational but the bodies it makes can help OTK or defend yourself.

YCS Chile and YCS Bologna Waiting Room

Are you excited for this new Toon format, or are you collecting the newer support cards for past decks? From those highly sought after serialized Grand Master Rares to the Extended Art cards and Starlights, or even down at the bargain bin with the Chibi variant artworks, these sets have it all for collectors and competitors.

As for how these newer cards are impacting the metagame? We're already seeing Toon and Unchained getting a lot of Regional-level success this past weekend with Blue-Eyes and Rokkets sneaking in too. Maybe players haven't solved the Spellcaster deck yet with the new Witchcrafter cards but the potential for them is pretty high. We'll have to wait and see what happens at next weekend's YCS Chile!

item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Magic: The Gathering This Week - 11/19/2026
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Magic: The Gathering This Week - 11/19/2026

You could say these Star Trek cards are soaring to new (competitive) heights.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Nov 19, 2026

|

5 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

How about that Anthropological Mission deck?

Stefan Schütz won the Magic World Championship last weekend, defeating Eduardo Sajgalik in a thrilling finals match to cap off what can only be described as a perfect weekend of Magic. Eight different Standard decks in the Top 8, 20,000-plus people at MagicCon: Atlanta, and three legends inducted into the Magic Pro Tour Hall of Fame class to remind us why we do all of this in the first place. All in all, it was impossible to ask for any more out of Magic.

Plus, the winning deck really delivered.

We've seen plenty of Izzet decks over the last few years, including several banned cards like Cori-Steel Cutter and Vivi Ornitier. And this time around the core spells of those lists are back again, this time with the new Star Trek standout Anthropological Mission as the payoff. Game after game, Schütz would deploy the enchantment on the third turn and begin drawing extra cards off it as early as the fourth. His removal-heavy deck was perfectly positioned against the many creature-heavy decks of the format, and his triumph in the finals was a stomp through the Llanowar Elves.

And the price of the new uncommon? It catapulted from under a dollar up to $6. That's not completely unheard of for an uncommon, but it's been some time since we've seen that kind of leap. Still, with no other major events to disrupt the progression from here, the default top deck of the current Standard format must again be Izzet. That said, there are plenty of options for disruption in the Mission deck, particularly, Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker. The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles rare is still under a dollar, so it may be worth grabbing your set while you can since it will be legal and very good against Anthropological Mission decks for the next two years.

There were actually two breakout uncommons from Star Trek, and The Naked Time may actually be the more lasting of the two. The powerful red enchantment was discovered by much of the field but seized on by very few – many top teams dismissed what ultimately became the most-played deck as well as one of the best-performing.

But combined with the power of Nurturing Pixie and an aggressive shell around it, the Boros Pixie deck enjoyed a huge breakout weekend and really showcased the power of The Naked TIme, which more or less did it all in the deck. As a result, this Star Trek uncommon also spiked, albeit from 50 cents to $3. Definitely a pair of uncommons to go back and look through your Prerelease bulk for.

This was the biggest financial winner of the Boros Pixie deck. After vomiting your hand onto the table with your aggressive start, Captain James T. Kirk is really the perfect card for the top end. It gives you the ability to pump the team for a final swing, or to reload on cards if you need it, or to put two bodies onto the board. And, of course, when things are really rolling for the Pixie deck? It does all three.

As a mythic rare from Star Trek, it had more room to grow than anything else mentioned so far, and grow it has. After settling down to just $4 after the Prerelease, old Tiberius is now up to a Market Price of exactly $20, a massive gain for a card you might see at the top end of red decks for the foreseeable future.

Speaking of Star Trek winners, Deep Space 9 may not have seen much play at the World Championship, but there's clearly interest coming from somewhere because the Market Price has climbed in the past 10 days from $20 all the way up to $35. It's very rare to see such gains in the release week of a set (honestly, we see it more in Pokémon than we do in Magic outside of something like the World Championship spiking prices), but Deep Space 9 appears to have been an early sleeper regardless of whether the demand is coming from Standard or Commander or just the Deep Space Nine television fans among us. 

And while we're talking Spacecraft cards, the extended art printing of Exploration Broodship has shown real growth, climbing from $4 to $6 in the last week. On that note, the extended art of Uthros Research Craft is still shooting up in price, going from $4 at the beginning of the month up to $11 and counting today. 

The Borg have arrived in Magic (I wonder if they'll ever meet the Phyrexians on the battlefield?), and they're already assimilating Urza, Chief Artificer into all of their decks. There's two printings of the Commander: The Brothers' War mythic rare, and both have leapt up in price over the last week. 

With a retro frame and an extended art printing, you could have purchased either one for around $5-7 a few weeks ago. But over the last week both have jumped, and you're now looking to spend at least $15 to pick up a copy. If you are building Borg, it's probably worth it.

The Best of the Rest

I love this card; it's one of the ones that first drew me to Magic, since I started playing in this block, and Merfolk is still my favorite deck. The price on this quirky enchantment has been a little wonky recently – it was going for almost $20 a few months ago before plummeting down to $11 or so, but it's been climbing since the beginning of the month. Merrow Commerce is up to $14 again, and really this all hinges on whether or not the enchantment is reprinted in Nauctis: The Sunken Realm. 

Somewhat similar is Mockingbird, or at least the showcase printing of it. The card is good enough to show up in several archetypes in Modern from time to time, and will always find a home in Commander. More recently, it's also begun finding new homes in Legacy, and the showcase printing has climbed from $6 to $9 in the last several weeks.

We'll end this week with another Reality Fracture jump. Jace, the Living Guildpact is benefitting from the same Jace hysteria that drove several other cards up in price while adding a new busted four-drop jace in The Theorist, Jace Beleren, but the Living Guildpact is just a few weeks behind the rest. I understand that Star Trek is already out, but Reality Fracture had a super compressed release window (I would assume so Star Trek could be out for the start of the holiday shopping season in the United States), and I don't think players are done building with Reality Fracture yet. To wit, Jace, the Living Guildpact climbed more this week, now up to almost an $8 Market Price from $3 at the beginning of the month.

item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|Commander|budget|casual

How To Upgrade All Four Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Decks

Space, the final frontier.

By Jason Coles

|

Published Nov 19, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Commander Upgrade

There are four Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek  Commander Decks, and each of them brings with it a mix of powerful new cards, excellent reprints, and sci-fi artwork. All four decks are helmed by a classic character from the franchise, and then filled to the brim with other fan favorites. While the decks are solid out of the box, you might want to take advantage of our guides to make them even better. 

Where To Find Every Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Upgrade Guide

You're going to have a good time with any of these decks. Each has a different gameplay focus: drawing cards, blatant violence, or swiping your opponent's creatures. Read on to find out which one is right for you, and then see how you can make them strong enough to tackle more decks in your playgroup. 

Federation Fleet

The main Commander for this blue, red, and white deck is, of course, Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary. Picard is a four-mana 2/4 that allows you to draw a card whenever an artifact, legendary, or saga enters the battlefield under your control. Then when you draw your second card you get to put a +1/+1 counter on another creature and two charge counters on a spacecraft. There are a lot of cards in this deck that benefit from drawing extra cards, and a lot of historic permanents too, so you'll get a lot of value out of this. 

The other option is Captain Janeway, Endgame. Also costing four-mana, this one is all about officers. When one hits a player, you get to draw a card and create a 1/1 officer token. On top of that, you can pay two mana and tap a creature you control to make Janeway unblockable. That offers the chance to move into a Voltron-style strategy, with cards like Picard making her stronger, and then you can just keep swinging in. 

Landing Party

Landing Party is in green, white, and blue, and sees a return to landfall. Unlike a lot of previous decks though, there's a big focus on lands with different names, so it really pays to have options in the deck. Commander Spock is a five-mana 3/5 that triggers when it enters or attacks. You then reveal the top card of your library, and can cast it if it's mana value is equal or less than the number of differently named lands you control. If it's a land, you can just put it into play. If neither of those happen, you get to draw a card.

Captain Kirk, Boldly Going is the second-in-command here as a four-mana 3/4 with vigilance that gives your spacecraft creatures +3/+3. You'll want to add more spacecraft to the deck if you want to focus on that aspect. Kirk also triggers on entry or attack, and lets you find the Starship Enterprise from your library or graveyard and put it into your hand. It's almost surgically niche, but it's a fun way to play things. 

Klingon Fury

Klingon Fury asks if you're angry, and then punches you in the face either way. This red, white, and black deck has Worf, Defiant Commander up front, which makes a 2/1 Klingon warrior with haste as it enters. When Worf attacks, you can exile cards from the top of your library equal to the number of people you attacked during that turn, and you can play them until the end of your next turn. It's card draw, but also angry about the whole thing. 

Kor, Cause of Vengeance is a four-mana 4/4 that lets you sacrifice another creature when you attack. If you do so, you get to not only draw a card, but give all of your Klingons and warriors +2/+2 until the end of the turn. The whole deck is all-in on Klingons, warriors, and attacking stuff, so it all works together quite smoothly. It's also designed to be used against everyone else at once, and you can get some tasty buffs for doing so. 

We Are The Borg 

The most evil of the decks is We Are The Borg. This white, blue, and black deck features artifact creatures and thievery. The Borg Queen comes in at a whopping seven mana, but this 4/4 gives all of your artifact creatures +2/+2, including itself. Plus, when it enters or attacks, you can exile cards from someone else's library until you hit a creature, then assimilate it onto your team. It's a nasty mix of abilities that ensures you're always getting stronger while potentially stripping away key cards from other people. 

Locutus of Borg is cheaper at four-mana, and is a 3/3 with lifelink. This one makes it so that every time an artifact creature you control hits an opponent, you get to make a 1/1 borg token. There's a very strong theme of going wide in the deck with multiple buffs and token generators that can do a lot of work. It's still a very combat-heavy deck, but with a bit more oomph than the others.

item.title: The 10 Cards Everybody Wants from The Dominance of God (OP-18)
item.description:
One Piece|collecting

The 10 Cards Everybody Wants from The Dominance of God (OP-18)

The saints are marching in.

By Joshua Calixto

|@HiThereJosh
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

3 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: The Cards Everybody Wants

The Dominance of God (OP-18) may not be an anniversary set or a heroines-themed special, but it packs in enough One Piece Card Game firsts to rack up similar levels of hype.

From Manga Robin, to a never-before-seen Straw Hat Leader, to a lineup of incredible alt-art cards, here are the cards everyone wants from The Dominance of God. 

#10 Mr. 0 and Miss All Sunday Alt-Art

The early-series villains make their joint debut on this super-powerful alt. Not only does this card buff a blue Baroque Works Leader to 7000 power on the opponent's turn, it also draws 2 cards on play and can attach 2 rested DON!! to your Leader and Characters, meaning it can essentially refund its own cost when played. If it's not sought-after for its art, it will be for its sheer potency.

#9 Monster Chopper Alt-Art

Although this card is just a normal alt-art (albeit for a card that fits perfectly into the new Green Luffy deck), it's the first alt-art card we've seen of Chopper in his Monster Point form. Even if it doesn't fetch the highest sale prices, we expect this one to be popular with collectors.

#8 Mr.2.Bon.Kurei(Bentham) Treasure Rare

Region-exclusive Treasure Rares can be hit or miss depending on the character, but this one features Bon Kurei disguised as Nami. EB-01 did something similar with the classic Purple Bon Kurei SEC alt-art, so expect this card to draw the combined appeal of a Nami card and a Bon Kurei card.

#7 I'll Make the Call SP Event

One Piece's SP Events have always been some of its most visually striking, and this Gunko-centric SP is absolutely gorgeous, with a striking black background that comes to life in the light as the textures show their full elegance.

#6 Loki Alt-Art by Yoshitaka Amano

OP-17 had guest art from Baki the Grappler artist Keisuke Itagaki, and OP-18 brings two guest entries from legendary Final Fantasy character artist Yoshitaka Amano.

Amano's first guest piece is a reprint of the Loki SEC from OP-17, and it also comes in a fancy Gold Parallel version.

#5 Saint Shamrock Alt-Art by Yoshitaka Amano

This Saint Shamrock alt-art isn't an SP like Loki, but it does come in a rarer version modeled on the "demon pack" Five Elders from OP-13, with a special metallic border and a pentagram around the card's cost.

#4 Franky Alt-Art Leader

The suuuuuuper long-awaited Franky Leader makes his first appearance in OP-18, and three years' worth of unsatisfied fans will finally get their chance to collect his alt-art Leader. Rendered in the set's mural-esque alt-art Leader style, this may not be one of the rarer hits in The Dominance of God, but it'll certainly be one of the most popular.

#3 Saint Gunko Holy Knights of God Super Alt-Art

Like the Pirate Crew alt-arts that were introduced in OP-17, this detailed Gunko Character card features the Holy Knights of God in the background, rendered in a similar style. The original Pirate Crew alts were some of the most sought-after cards in The World's Strongest Warriors, and we expect this one to be just as popular. 

#2 Saint Gunko Super Alt-Art (Manga) Leader

Super Alt-Art Leader cards premiered in OP-17 with Elbaph Luffy, and have proven to be some of the most sought-after chases ever since, with EB-05 Robin fetching similar levels of attention. The Dominance of God (OP-18) sees the debut of Saint Gunko, a fan-favorite antagonist from the Elbaph arc, and her Super Alt-Art card is poised to be one of the biggest chases of the set.

#1 Manga Nico Robin

Nico Robin has always been a One Piece fan-favorite character, and OP-18 gives her her first-ever Manga Rare. Considering the last few sets featured Shirahoshi and the original Four Emperors as their Mangas (which are popular, but not Robin popular), Robin is slated to be one of the most hyped Manga Rares the One Piece Card Game has ever seen.
